extracted.intended_audience: Catholic children and learners preparing for catechism or instruction in basic Catholic doctrine
extracted.subtask_description: A pedagogical catechism in question-and-answer form covering death, judgment, Heaven, Hell, Purgatory, and a broad series of doctrinal and moral questions for lessons. Intended as a learner's exam/recitation and teacher's guide for basic Catholic instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation for the Particular Judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person should prepare for the judgment they undergo immediately after death by examining their conscience on sins committed, making an act of contrition, resolving to avoid future sin, and becoming better acquainted with Christ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: 'You should never go to sleep without some preparation for judgment.' Examples: examine conscience daily, make an act of contrition, resolve to avoid sins, pray and perform good works to become Christ's friend so that at judgment you will be 'pleased rather than afraid to meet Him.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and Nature of the Particular Judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The judgment a person undergoes immediately after death is called the Particular Judgment — 'Particular,' because one particular person is judged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that at that moment the soul 'sees in an instant its own state and knows what its sentence will be' and 'goes immediately to its reward or punishment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and Purpose of the General Judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Judgment is the judgment all men (and angels/devils) will undergo on the last day — 'General,' because every creature gifted with intelligence will be judged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive signs (earthquakes, seas raging, sun darkened, trumpet call), the dead rising, separation of the good and wicked, public revelation of deeds. Stated purposes: to make God's providence and justice plain before all, to show the crimes of sinners and justice of their punishment, to reveal and glorify the saints' works, and for the honor and glory of Our Lord.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-judgment Destinations (Heaven, Purgatory, Hell)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Particular Judgment souls are appointed to one of three states: Heaven, Purgatory, or Hell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple listing with explanatory notes: Heaven as everlasting vision of God; Purgatory as temporary suffering for venial sins or unsatisfied temporal punishment; Hell as eternal deprivation of the sight of God and sense-torments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and Sufferings of Hell
rubrics_metrics.description: Hell is a state of eternal deprivation of the sight of God (the pain of loss) and of dreadful torments of the senses (the pain of sense).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes distinction between pain of loss (greatest torment) and pain of sense; warns that human descriptions understate reality; preachers should expand upon 'absence of everything good and the presence of everything evil' to instill holy fear and sorrow for sin. Lists absent goods (light, hope, friendship) and social consequences (hatred among damned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and Purpose of Purgatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Purgatory is the state in which those who die guilty of venial sins, or without having satisfied temporal punishment, suffer for a time to be cleansed before entering Heaven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that Purgatory involves pains of sense similar to Hell but endured willingly because they purify; the salvation of those in Purgatory is sure. Practical guidance: the faithful on earth may shorten the time of souls there by prayers, good works, indulgences, and Masses said for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: How the Faithful Can Help Souls in Purgatory
rubrics_metrics.description: The faithful on earth can assist souls in Purgatory by prayers, fasts, almsdeeds, indulgences, and having Masses said for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promises that helping souls is a 'great charity' and that those helped will pray for their benefactors when admitted into Heaven; also suggests a spiritual reciprocity in prayers at death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resurrection and the Bodies' Participation in Reward or Punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the Resurrection the bodies will again be united to souls and will share in the reward or punishment assigned to the soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that bodies of the just 'will rise glorious and immortal' and that even the bodies of the damned 'will also rise' but be condemned to eternal punishment; explains respectful burial practices because of the future resurrection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heaven and the Beatific Vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Heaven is everlasting life in which we see God face to face, are made like unto Him in glory, and enjoy eternal happiness; the vision of God is called the 'beatific vision.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that seeing God 'as He is' requires a special 'light of glory' given by God; human analogies fall short and imagined pleasures of earth do not compare to Heaven's reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Exhortation to Use the Present to Merit Heaven
rubrics_metrics.description: The present life is the only time to merit Heaven and avoid Hell; one should daily consider where one would stand if judgment occurred today and act to make amends for past faults as well as resolve to be better in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses the Lord's words: 'What doth it profit a man if he gain the whole world and suffer the loss of his own soul?' Advises daily self-examination, repentance, amendment, and active effort to 'make up for what we have neglected in the past.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical Format: Question-and-Answer Structure for Catechetical Instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The catechism is organized as numbered questions and concise answers for use in lessons and examination; omissions in some answers are intentional because material is explained elsewhere or is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note to teacher/reader: 'The explanations of such questions or answers can be easily found by referring to the index.' The Q&A list (many specific doctrinal/moral items) functions as an instructional checklist for lesson planning and student recitation.
